status: STRUCTURE RATIFIED; MEASURED FIELDS ARE GENERATED. Every exact model version owns separate evidence: predecessor scores, vetoes, and verdicts never transfer. Todd ratified the 14-dimension list, the coarse ordinal -4..+3 scale and user-level placement on 2026-07-24. Cost and speed are now measured for BOTH harnesses (Claude reports dollars; Codex is token-derived) and the `measured` block on every config plus the `measuredAt` stamp are REGENERATED by .orchestrator/matrix-refresh.ps1 — never hand-edit them. Authored content (cell scores, vetoes, bars, provenance) is human-maintained under the citable-source rule and is left untouched by refresh. New-work selection is resolved from routing-policy family slots and the AgentPools model registry at dispatch time; current swaps create a distinct exact `<current>/<effort>` configuration and never copy predecessor evidence. The SKILL.md routing mechanism describes this data binding; this file is the numbers of record.

costPipeline.1-harvest: .orchestrator/cost-harvest.ps1 — transcripts -> cost-ledger.jsonl. Idempotent; opens transcripts share-read so it never contends with a live lane. Claude reports total_cost_usd; Codex reports cumulative run tokens, from which the harvester records billed-at-the-time and current-price-normalized USD plus short/long context bounds. Runs above 272K cumulative input use a labeled conservative long-tier upper bound because per-request tier is unavailable.
costPipeline.2-refresh: .orchestrator/matrix-refresh.ps1 — regenerates every `measured` block and the `measuredAt` stamp from the ledger + dispatch log. Routing comparisons use current-price-normalized USD so historical token traces are evaluated at today's prices; operational spend retains billed-at-the-time USD. Requires exact model versions, excludes aliases/deprecated/ambiguous identities, and aliases only row/routingRow spellings before grouping. Run after every harvest.
costPipeline.3-report: .orchestrator/cost-harvest.ps1 -Summary — cost and duration by model for the window; routing joins use canonical lifecycle rows.
costPipeline.adjudicate: matrix-refresh.ps1 -Adjudicate freezes current values as the drift baseline. Only at a recompute, only after a human has looked — never automatically.
costPipeline.driftAlarm: Any measured value moving >=25% from its adjudicated baseline is reported. Auto-update without drift detection just hides the change; this surfaces the moment a routing choice may have flipped.

scope: coarse ordinal -4..+3 scale over continuous scoring
user-level placement in the skill dir (no git history; cell-edit discipline rests on the citable-source rule, not on review)
ratified.notRatified: Cell VALUES are not ratified — they are seeded from external benchmarks and small-n local measurement, and carry provenance letters accordingly. Structure is agreed; numbers remain under challenge.

scale.meaning: Each cell scores a config against the dimension's named baseline config, which may be historical and nonselectable. 0 = as good as that baseline. Positive = better. Negative = measurably worse than that baseline. Units are deliberately coarse ordinal steps, not benchmark points — benchmarks are not commensurable across dimensions.

steps.+3: decisively better; would displace the baseline on capability alone
steps.+2: clearly better on the governing evidence
steps.+1: better, or equal at materially lower cost
steps.-2: materially worse; fallback only under constraint, budget an extra repair round
steps.-3: poor fit; needs an explicit reason to route here

scale.veto: A vetoed config is INELIGIBLE AT ANY PRICE. Vetoes are categorical, never scalar — a large negative number can be outweighed by cheapness in step 4, a veto cannot. Use veto when running the config is worse than not doing the task at all, or when a hard constraint (governance, classifier reroute, context collapse) applies.
scale.null: UNKNOWN — no source. Routes CONSERVATIVELY, never optimistically. An unknown cell is not a zero and must never be selected over a known-clearing cell.

provenance.M: Measured here — chase-sets dispatch-log join. Carries n. Preferred over all other sources.
provenance.B: External benchmark on this dimension's governing evidence.
provenance.V: Vendor claim or positioning. Weakest source; treat as a hypothesis to test, never as clearing a bar on its own.

rules.cellEdit: A cell may only be changed with a citable source tied to the exact model version: a dispatch-log join (M) or a published benchmark (B). Log the edit with its source. Editing a cell to justify a routing choice already made turns this file into a rationalization engine.
rules.versionIdentity: Every exact model version is a new config with empty evidence cells. Never transfer a predecessor's score, veto, benchmark result, block rate, cost rate, or qualitative verdict. Exclude ambiguous family aliases and historical rows whose exact reported model version cannot be proven.
rules.preferMeasured: When two cells clear the bar, prefer the one with M provenance over B over V.
rules.smallN: With n < 8, use the lower confidence bound, not the point estimate. Fable's deep-repo baseline rests on n=8 — a ceiling, not a target.
rules.provisional: Cells sourced from B or V on a config with no measured history are PROVISIONAL, never automatic promotion authority and never a tier-3 rung on an irreversible artifact. Host selection requires the operator under row 9; successor host arms retain provisional evidence labels without automatic rotation. At recompute, use only the current row's eligible configuration; a retired historical baseline is never a fallback. Successor continuity defaults remain provisional until their own evidence supports reviewed rebalance.
rules.laneBinding: Claude lanes run Claude configs, Codex lanes run GPT-6 configs. This filters the candidate set BEFORE scoring; it is a constraint, not a capability dimension. Historical GPT-5.6 configs never become selectable through lane binding. Work conservation never admits a below-bar or protected-scope-ineligible configuration.
rules.generatedVsAuthored: GENERATED (never hand-edit): every config's `measured` block and the top-level `measuredAt` stamp. AUTHORED (human, citable-source rule): cell scores, vetoes, bars, provenance letters, notes, dimension definitions. Hand-copied numbers go stale within a day and hide sampling bugs. Exact-version enforcement now excludes aliases rather than guessing them into a version bucket.

rules.v413EffortConfiguration: Todd 2026-09-08 (v4.13): the routing unit is a configuration (exact model + exact effort). matrix-refresh.ps1 keys every measured block by both: a run's effort is its dispatch row joined on the transcript (effortUsed over effort), else the <issue>-<model>-<effort>- transcript-name token; a receipt's author effort is its authorEffort field (log-event.ps1 -AuthorEffort), else the author's own dispatch rows up to the receipt instant when they agree. Unresolved or ambiguous rows count for the model and the row but for no configuration, and are reported in measuredAt.effortIdentity. A config with no effort-resolved run carries no measured block; per-model pooled figures live only in measuredAt.byModel. Quota thresholds and rebalance comparisons read measuredAt.byRowConfig and measuredAt.blockRateByRowConfig; byRowModel and blockRateByRow answer per-model questions only. An effort step on the incumbent's model is a challenger like any other (row-4 Sol medium quota). Effort is ordinal within a model's authored ladder (effortLadders) and never comparable across models; price bands are reporting labels, never routing inputs.
rules.v413ConfigIdVersion: Todd 2026-09-08 (v4.13): a configuration is two-dimensional (exact model selector + effort) and its id is DERIVED, never named: <exact selector>/<effort> (gpt-6-astra/high, gpt-5.6-sol/high, claude-fable-5-1/high). matrix-refresh.ps1 refuses a config whose id is not exactly its canonical model + '/' + effort, so an id can never drift from the configuration it keys and a successor version can never inherit a predecessor's key. decisionProcedure: 0. Apply Todd's 2026-09-12 authorship rule before dimension scoring: copywriting (including user-facing localization), all design-system changes, and architectural-core design/implementation/repair require Fable 5.1 or Astra at the SKILL.md row-7/14/15 configurations. Architectural core covers domain foundations, shared platform contracts, and execution authority as defined in SKILL.md. Routine consumers of established contracts remain ordinary implementation; split mixed tasks. These standing placements are override-Todd policy, not capability evidence.
1. Classify the task into one or more dimensions. Composite tasks (e.g. deep-repo change touching money) take the MAX bar across their dimensions and must clear every one.
2. Filter retiredModels and configs with selectable:false before lane binding and governance, context, rate-limit and latency gates. Spend is telemetry, never a gate.
3. Drop every vetoed config, and every config whose gate conditions are triggered.
4. Keep configs whose score >= the dimension's bar-equivalent; with small n use the lower confidence bound. Never select a null cell over a known-clearing cell.
5. Among survivors pick the LOWEST current-price-normalized usdPerRun — not the highest score. Correctness is the FILTER (step 4), cost is the CHOICE (step 5).

6. SPEED is the tie-breaker, and overrides step 5 when the pipeline is waiting: if something is blocked behind this lane, prefer the lower generated medianMin even at higher cost. Never repeat measured rankings or values in authored prose; read the current generated blocks.
7. Log the chosen config, dimension, score, and the cell's provenance letter. Second-cheapest survivor is the documented fallback.

threeAxes.correctness: cell score vs the dimension's bar — a FILTER, never traded against cost. A config below the bar is not eligible at any price.
threeAxes.cost: usdPerRun, measured at current prices. Both harnesses are covered: Claude reports dollars; Codex is repriced from historical token traces using current short/long price tables. Historical runs above 272K cumulative input use a labeled conservative long-tier upper bound because per-request context tier cannot be reconstructed. Billed-at-the-time USD is retained separately for spend governance.
threeAxes.speed: medianMin per run, plus usdPerMin. Claude durations are measured; Codex emits no wall-clock so its durations are file-span estimates.
threeAxes.denominatorWarning: A RUN is not a fixed unit of work, and per-run and per-minute rankings can disagree. Always state which denominator a comparison uses and derive the relationship from the current generated blocks.

barMeaning.85: Internal draft. Externally validated downstream (review, CI) before it reaches anyone.
barMeaning.95: User-visible, or lands without a further human read.
barMeaning.99: Material operational action or expensive-to-reverse. Requires independent verification and a rollback path.
barMeaning.human: Regulated or irreversible. Human approval plus audit trail; the model never decides alone.

coverage.note: A mostly-empty honest matrix beats a full fabricated one. Null cells route conservatively and are the work-list for the next recompute.

openGaps: CODEX COST IS DERIVED, NOT REPORTED — it is only as accurate as cost-harvest.ps1. The harvester must preserve billed-at-the-time USD while repricing every historical token trace at current short/long rates for routing. Historical telemetry is cumulative per run rather than per request, so >272K runs carry bounds and a conservative long-tier point. A price change that misses any tier or effective-dated table silently corrupts one use. Re-check them at each recompute and whenever a GPT-5.6 price moves.
Codex emits no wall-clock, so its durations are file-span estimates (creation->last-write). Treat Codex medianMin as approximate; Claude durations are measured.

Some harvested spend does not join to a routing row when the issue is absent from the filename or no dispatch row matches. Read `measuredAt.usdNotJoinedToRow` for the current amount. The `transcript` field on dispatch rows fixes this forward; history stays partly unattributed.

Effort identity is resolved, not reported: the ledger carries no effort, so matrix-refresh.ps1 joins it from the dispatch row on the transcript or parses the transcript-name token, and receipts before v4.13 carry no authorEffort so their author configuration comes from the author's dispatch rows. Read measuredAt.effortIdentity for the unresolved and ambiguous counts each refresh; a configuration listed in measuredAt.configsWithoutEffortEvidence has no cost cell and routes as unknown.

A run is not an artifact: read row cost and sample size from `measuredAt.byRow`; an artifact may span several runs plus review and repair. True USD/artifact needs run-to-artifact grouping the ledger does not yet do.

Opus 5 vs Sol on agentic-coding and long-horizon-execution rests on public B cells (Terminal-Bench 4.0, Agents' Last Exam, AutomationBench) as of 2026-09-07; no local M comparison exists. The Astra high quota on rows 4, 5, and 10 supplies the next M cells at the rebalance.

Opus 5 review recall and precision: P5/P6 resolved 2026-09-07 on CodeRabbit's model-level results plus local reviewer block tendency. No exact claude-opus-5/high vs claude-sonnet-5/medium precision pair exists, so the review-precision cell for claude-opus-5/high stays null until local M; the review-recall cell for claude-opus-5/high is a B cell against Sol's 69.7%.

Opus 5 writing Elo is known (arena text claude-opus-5-high 1493 vs Fable 5 1507). Design Elo exists only at max effort on the WebDev arena for Astra, Fable 5.1, and Opus 5; the high-effort ui-design cells for Astra and Fable 5.1 stay null.
volume-extraction has no internal gold set, so its bar cannot be evaluated locally.
Block rates are difficulty-confounded (Sol and Fable draw the full-path work); cells sourced from them need stratification before they can be trusted across dimensions.
dispatch-log uses both `row` (1363) and `routingRow` (57) for the same concept — any join silently drops the stragglers.

measuredAt.effortIdentityNote: A run's effort is the dispatch row joined on its transcript (effortUsed over effort), else the <issue>-<model>-<effort>- transcript-name token; a receipt's author effort is its authorEffort field, else the author's own dispatch rows up to the receipt instant when they agree. Unresolved or ambiguous rows count for the model and the row but for no configuration.
measuredAt.outcomeNote: Indeterminate outcomes (RETRY, skip, LOAD_SENSITIVE, GREEN_LOAD_DISCRIMINATED, BLOCKED_ON_PRODUCT_DEFECTS, TIMEOUT_ONLY_*) are excluded from the denominator, not scored as passes.
measuredAt.mechanicalNote: Mechanical failures (BLOCK_MECHANICAL, MECHANICAL_PROMPT_BLOCK, FAILED_CLEAN_MAIN) are excluded from author block rate: they measure the harness, not the author. Counting them as blocks biases every per-config rate upward.
measuredAt.modelIdentityNote: Version-EXPLICIT spellings (sonnet-5, 'Sonnet 5') are normalized onto their canonical id: the version is carried through, never inferred. Bare family aliases (sonnet, fable, opus) and deprecated versions remain excluded rather than mapped onto a successor.
measuredAt.generatedBy: .orchestrator/matrix-refresh.ps1 — do NOT hand-edit any measured block or this stamp

effortLadders.$comment: Authored routing ladders; retired predecessor ladders remain for historical interpretation only. Live pool verified 2026-09-22: low minimum, no none/minimal. Sol ultra advertised but not qualified for incumbent routing. Claude-native Opus 5.5 xhigh is distinct; Responses translates xhigh/max to upstream max, so evidence must name the harness. Sonnet 5.5 native Claude Code 2.1.284 admission passed all five efforts on 2026-09-28; its Responses translator also collapses xhigh/max to upstream max. Sol 6.1 (OpenAI model page 2026-09-29) offers low through max with no none/minimal; installed Codex CLI 0.159.0 admitted low through ultra, and ultra stays unqualified for incumbent routing.

priceBands.$comment: Reporting label only, derived from short-context input list price; never a routing input and never a claim about model size, which is unobservable. Models in one band are not interchangeable (Sol and Opus 5 win different rows).
